body:
On a Linux HPC environment, importing torch failed with
`ImportError: libnccl.so.2: cannot open shared object file`.
`nvidia_nccl_cu13-2.30.7.dist-info` existed and its `RECORD` listed
`nvidia/nccl/lib/libnccl.so.2` at 252,204,648 bytes, but the entire
`nvidia/nccl/` directory was absent. Repeating `uv sync --frozen` did not
restore it or report the missing library.

`uv sync --frozen --reinstall-package nvidia-nccl-cu13` restored the library
at the recorded size. Our setup script now checks `import torch` before
marking the environment verified, and the package cache has been moved
away from the quota-limited home filesystem.

The home filesystem was full around the incident. That is a suspected
trigger, not an established cause: we did not preserve the original
installation output, exact uv/Python versions, or a reproducer of the file
loss. We cannot establish whether installation, a corrupt cache, or a later
operation removed the files. The observed behavior is that a subsequent
sync accepted the incomplete environment. Is there a supported way to
detect missing installed files without forcing a reinstall?

Related reports checked before drafting:

- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/16468 describes missing package files
  after remove/add on macOS, but also a missing RECORD; our RECORD existed.
- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/19683 was closed after a clean cache
  resolved missing files. We have not established whether that cause applies.
title: uv sync leaves an environment with missing NCCL library unchanged
